message.content:
For a garden sculpture you’ll want a stone that balances **carvability** with **weather‑resistance**.  
The classic choice is **marble** – it has a fine, uniform grain that makes it easy to carve intricate details, yet it’s still hard enough to hold up outdoors when properly sealed.  

Other good options include:

| Stone | Carvability | Weather‑Resistance | Typical Use |
|-------|-------------|--------------------|-------------|
| **Marble** | Excellent | Good (needs sealing) | Classic garden statues |
| **Granite** | Harder to carve | Excellent | Large, durable pieces |
| **Limestone** | Very easy to carve | Moderate (can erode) | Softer, more rustic look |
| **Sandstone** | Easy to carve | Poor (softest) | Rarely used for long‑term outdoor art |

So if you’re looking for the most suitable rock for a garden sculpture, **marble** is usually the top pick. It offers the right mix of detail work and longevity, especially when treated with a proper sealant to protect against rain and temperature swings.
